prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1179; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the claimant reported a low-speed collision in a parking lot and a neck injury diagnosed as whiplash. The claimant is not represented by an attorney, so all contact will be direct.

Entry 2: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the vehicles made contact in the lot the way the claimant described. Both parties agree on the sequence of events.

Entry 3: Obtained statements from two witnesses and photos of both vehicles. The witnesses and photos match the reported impact, and the damage appears largely consistent with it.

Entry 4: Police report lists the claimant as a passenger in the vehicle at the time of the collision, which matches the claimant's account. The policyholder confirmed the driver lives in the household and is listed as a covered member.

Entry 5: The claimant's medical records show treatment that followed a typical course for this type of injury, with visits tapering off as symptoms improved. No prior injury to the neck or upper back appears in the records.

Entry 6: Prior-loss records turned up a claim involving major damage to the same areas of the vehicle from an earlier accident that was never reported to us. The current claim presents that damage as new, so this needs to be reconciled before any payment decision.

Entry 7: The claimant later added a few smaller details, such as the position of the other car and how long the vehicles stayed in contact, but the core account has not changed. Nothing in the file suggests the damage happened before the policy's coverage start date.

Entry 8: Reviewed the file and noted the open question about the earlier unreported damage. Next step is to request the prior repair estimate and speak with the claimant about that history before closing the injury and property portions of the claim.
